subfamily: a grapefruit sour after Arnold's Shaken Drake (Liquid Intelligence p. 149): the grapefruit juice frozen into cubes is the ice, shaken to slush, so the melt is juice, not water
version: v2 (Tomás, round 4; story ruled by Wren r3). Freeform because no water is added: the grapefruit is the ice. Judged by hand against Arnold's shaken (sours) finished ranges, with stray-melt cases of 10 and 20 ml water in the sweep. Malört at the US liqueur sugar floor (2.4 g/100 ml); maple 1 tsp.

ingredients.note: Jeppson's Malört (35%), recommended; or any Swedish besk (beskbrännvin, bitter wormwood spirit) of 35% or stronger
fresh white grapefruit juice, strained, frozen ahead in two 30 ml ice cubes (Arnold's method)
1 teaspoon; Arnold uses maple to round out the bitterness of the grapefruit (LI p. 149)
or a generous pinch of fine salt (Arnold's own alternative, p. 149)

_notes: Shake Malört, maple and salt with the two frozen grapefruit cubes, hard, until the cubes are slush (30 s at least, Arnold); strain into the frozen coupe. No other ice. Malört sugar unpublished: modelled at the legal liqueur floor (27 CFR 5.150, Hester r3), swept to 6 g/100 ml. Sweeps in work/regular-guy-jester/mixologist-sweep.py.
